metadata.name: agent_rails
metadata.description: Programmable spending rails for autonomous agents on Solana

instructions.name: add_allowlist_entry
docs: Approves one destination wallet for a policy (spec §5.2).

instructions.name: add_guardian
docs: Registers one guardian key (spec §5.1).

instructions.name: add_mint
docs: Configures a mint slot and its spending ceiling (spec §5.1).

accounts.name: owner
docs: Rent payer for a newly created vault ATA. Native SOL does not create one.

accounts.name: mint
docs: be an initialized mint owned by SPL Token or Token-2022; the handler enforces that
before reading decimals or extensions.

accounts.name: vault_ata
docs: Vault ATA for `(treasury, mint, token_program)`. Omitted for native SOL (spec §5.1).
by the Associated Token Account program, which is the authority on that PDA.

accounts.name: token_program
docs: SPL Token or Token-2022. Omitted for native SOL; the System program is stored
in `MintConfig.token_program` on that path instead.

accounts.name: associated_token_program
docs: Omitted for native SOL; required whenever `vault_ata` is created.

instructions.name: close_policy
docs: Reclaims a policy with no active sessions (spec §5.2).

accounts.name: rent_destination
docs: this account. Never read or written by the program beyond the lamport transfer.

instructions.name: close_receipt
docs: Permissionless receipt reclamation after expiry plus grace (spec §5.4).

accounts.name: fee_payer
docs: rent. The closer does not have to be this key.

instructions.name: close_session
docs: Reclaims a revoked or expired session's rent (spec §5.2).

accounts.name: rent_destination
docs: this account.

instructions.name: close_treasury
docs: Reclaims the treasury once every vault, policy, and session is gone (spec §5.1).

accounts.name: rent_destination
docs: would strand the floor lamports on a PDA nobody can sign for after close.

instructions.name: create_policy
docs: Creates a named rule set bounded by the treasury's ceilings (spec §5.2).

accounts.name: operator
docs: Operator or owner; also the rent payer. Checked in the handler because `has_one`
cannot express "either of two fields".

instructions.name: create_session
docs: Issues a time-boxed spending session to one agent key (spec §5.2).

instructions.name: create_treasury
docs: Creates a treasury and funds its native SOL vault to the rent floor (spec §5.1).

accounts.name: create_key
docs: Ephemeral keypair that seeds the treasury PDA. It signs exactly once, here, and is
then discarded — which is what lets one owner hold unlimited treasuries without the
program tracking an index.

accounts.name: sol_vault
docs: System-owned PDA with zero data bytes. It is never `init`ed as a program account:
lamports are simply transferred in, which leaves it spendable by
`system_program::transfer` with `invoke_signed` and keeps SOL payments cheap.

instructions.name: execute_payment
docs: Pays an SPL Token or Token-2022 amount from the vault, subject to the full policy
check sequence (spec §5.3).

accounts.name: fee_payer
docs: Pays receipt rent, and destination ATA rent if one is created. Separate from
`session_key` so an operator can sponsor fees today and a relayer can slot in for
v1.1 signed-intent mode without an account-layout change.

accounts.name: session_key
docs: The agent. `has_one` on `session` binds it to the registered key.

accounts.name: policy
docs: No `seeds` constraint, deliberately, and it is not a shortcut. `session` carries
`has_one = policy`, and `session.policy` is written only by `create_session` from a
policy that passed its own seeds check. `Account<Policy>` pins the owner and the
discriminator. Re-deriving `["policy", treasury, name]` here would re-prove something
already proven, at the cost of a `create_program_address` syscall on the hot path.

accounts.name: allowlist_entry
docs: Required exactly when `policy.destination_mode == Allowlist`. The handler verifies
the seeds rather than the derive macro, so an entry belonging to another policy
fails with `DestinationNotAllowed` instead of a raw seeds error.

accounts.name: vault_ata
docs: The vault. `associated_token::*` both derives the address and checks the
deserialized owner, so this is the treasury's canonical account for this mint.

accounts.name: destination_owner
docs: account is derived from it below and this account itself is never read or written.

accounts.name: destination_ata
docs: token_program)`. Left unchecked here because creating it is gated on
`policy.create_destination_ata`, which `init_if_needed` could not express: it would
create the account during account validation, before the policy has been consulted.

accounts.name: receipt
docs: The idempotency record. `init` is the entire mechanism: a replayed `intent_id`
collides here and the transaction dies before any transfer (ADR-004).

instructions.name: execute_payment_sol
docs: The same payment, in native SOL from `sol_vault` (spec §5.3).

accounts.name: policy
docs: No `seeds` constraint, deliberately, and it is not a shortcut. `session` carries
`has_one = policy`, and `session.policy` is written only by `create_session` from a
policy that passed its own seeds check. `Account<Policy>` pins the owner and the
discriminator. Re-deriving `["policy", treasury, name]` here would re-prove something
already proven, at the cost of a `create_program_address` syscall on the hot path.

accounts.name: allowlist_entry
docs: Required exactly when `policy.destination_mode == Allowlist`; seeds verified by the
handler.

accounts.name: destination_owner
docs: `SystemAccount` is the point: lamports may only be sent to a system-owned wallet,
never to a program-owned account this instruction could be tricked into writing.

instructions.name: pause
docs: Agent kill switch. Owner or a registered guardian (spec §5.1).

instructions.name: remove_allowlist_entry
docs: Withdraws that approval and reclaims its rent (spec §5.2).

accounts.name: policy
docs: address is pinned by `entry.policy`, and the handler checks `policy.treasury` when
the account is still live.

accounts.name: rent_destination
docs: this account.

instructions.name: remove_guardian
docs: Drops one guardian key (spec §5.1).

instructions.name: remove_mint
docs: Delists a mint whose vault is empty, freeing its slot (spec §5.1).

accounts.name: mint
docs: nothing here reads the mint's data — a mint whose account was somehow closed must
still be delistable.

accounts.name: vault_ata
docs: Required for SPL and Token-2022, omitted for native SOL. Deserialized so its
`amount` can be checked; the address is re-derived from the stored token program.

accounts.name: sol_vault
docs: Required for native SOL, omitted otherwise. Spec §5.1 lists only `vault_ata`, but the
native path has no token account and its emptiness check is "at the rent floor"
instead — so the two are mutually exclusive optionals.

instructions.name: revoke_session
docs: Stops one agent immediately and permanently (spec §5.2).

accounts.name: authority
docs: Owner or operator. Guardians can only pause, never reach into a session.

instructions.name: set_ceiling
docs: Moves the owner's bound on one mint, and the two destination flags (spec §5.1).

instructions.name: set_roles
docs: Rotates the owner and/or operator (spec §5.1).

instructions.name: unpause
docs: Restores agent payments. Owner-only (spec §5.1).

instructions.name: update_policy
docs: Rewrites a live policy's rules, still bounded by the ceiling (spec §5.2).

accounts.name: operator
docs: Operator or owner. Checked in the handler because `has_one` cannot express
"either of two fields".

accounts.name: treasury
docs: Read-only: an update changes no treasury state. `policy_count` is unaffected because
no policy is created or destroyed.

instructions.name: withdraw
docs: Owner withdrawal of vault funds, permitted while paused (spec §5.1).

accounts.name: treasury
docs: Read-only: the treasury signs the transfer as a PDA but is not mutated.

accounts.name: mint
docs: initialized mint; the handler unpacks it before the token CPI.

accounts.name: vault_ata
docs: Required for SPL / Token-2022, omitted for native SOL.

accounts.name: sol_vault
docs: Required for native SOL, omitted otherwise.

accounts.name: destination
docs: Token account for SPL, system account for SOL. Validated in the handler because
the two paths disagree on owner and layout.

accounts.name: token_program
docs: Required for SPL / Token-2022, omitted for native SOL.

types.name: AgentSession
docs: A revocable, time-boxed delegation of spending authority to one agent key
(spec §3.3). 588 bytes.
| Offset | Size | Field |
| 0 | 8 | discriminator |
| 8 | 1 | `version` |
| 10 | 32 | `treasury` |
| 74 | 32 | `session_key` |
| 106 | 1 | `auth_mode` |
| 139 | 8 | `created_at` |
| 147 | 8 | `expires_at` |
| 155 | 1 | `revoked` |
| 156 | 8 | `revoked_at` |
| 172 | 32 | `audit_head` |
| 524 | 64 | `reserved` |
PDA: `["session", treasury, session_key]`. Rotation means a new key, never a mutation.

fields.name: session_key
docs: Seed component, and the signer in `AuthMode::DirectSigner`.

fields.name: auth_mode
docs: `AuthMode`; must be 0 in v1.

fields.name: label
docs: Human label, e.g. `"billing-agent-prod"`.

fields.name: seq
docs: Executed payments; starts at 0 and increases by exactly 1 per payment.

fields.name: audit_head
docs: Head of the audit hash chain (spec §6).

fields.name: spend
docs: Index-aligned with `Policy.mint_limits` at creation, but always looked up by mint.

types.name: AllowlistEntry
docs: One approved destination for a policy (spec §3.4). 186 bytes.
| Offset | Size | Field |
| 0 | 8 | discriminator |
| 8 | 1 | `version` |
| 42 | 32 | `destination_owner` |
| 106 | 8 | `per_tx_max_override` |
| 154 | 32 | `reserved` |
PDA: `["allow", policy, destination_owner]`. Keyed by the wallet owner and never by a
token account, so one entry covers every mint.

fields.name: destination_owner
docs: Wallet owner (system account); the ATA is derived on-chain at payment time.

fields.name: label
docs: e.g. `"openai-billing"`.

fields.name: per_tx_max_override
docs: 0 means no override; otherwise it must be `≤` the policy's `per_tx_max`.

types.name: CeilingUpdated
docs: An owner-set ceiling changed (spec §8).
Both treasury-wide destination flags ride along because they are part of the same
bound: a policy is legal only if its limits fit the per-mint ceiling *and* its
destination mode fits these.

types.name: IntentReceipt
docs: The idempotency record for one payment intent (spec §3.5). 243 bytes.
| Offset | Size | Field |
| 0 | 8 | discriminator |
| 8 | 1 | `version` |
| 10 | 32 | `session` |
| 42 | 16 | `intent_id` |
| 90 | 32 | `destination_owner` |
| 146 | 8 | `timestamp` |
| 154 | 8 | `expires_at` |
| 163 | 32 | `fee_payer` |
| 195 | 32 | `memo_hash` |
| 227 | 16 | `reserved` |
PDA: `["receipt", session, intent_id]`.
The account *is* the idempotency mechanism (ADR-004): `execute_payment` `init`s it
before it transfers anything, so a retried intent fails at account creation rather than
paying twice. Nothing here is read back by the program on the payment path — the fields
exist so that `get_payment_status` can answer "did it land?" authoritatively, and so
`close_receipt` knows when the record may be reclaimed and by whom.

fields.name: intent_id
docs: Client-generated, UUIDv7 by default; the raw 16 bytes are also a seed component.

fields.name: amount
docs: Debited from the vault, before any Token-2022 transfer fee.

fields.name: seq
docs: The session's `seq` *after* this payment, so the receipt pins one link of the audit
chain and an indexer can reconstruct the order without the events.

fields.name: expires_at
docs: Copied from the intent. Gates `close_receipt`, so a receipt outlives its intent by
exactly `RECEIPT_GRACE_SECONDS`.

fields.name: status
docs: `ReceiptStatus`. Only `Executed` exists in v1: a receipt is written after the
transfer succeeds, and a failed payment leaves no account behind.

fields.name: fee_payer
docs: Rent refund target for `close_receipt`, recorded because whoever closes the receipt
is not necessarily whoever paid for it.

fields.name: memo_hash
docs: `sha256(memo)`, or all zeros when the memo is empty. The memo itself is never
stored: it is unbounded-ish caller data, and a commitment is enough to prove what
was submitted.

types.name: MintCeiling
docs: The owner's ceiling for one mint: the loosest limits any policy on this treasury may
set, and the shortest windows it may use (spec §3.1.1). 40 bytes.
| Offset | Size | Field |
| 0 | 8 | `max_per_tx` |
| 8 | 8 | `max_short_window` |
| 16 | 8 | `max_long_window` |
| 24 | 8 | `max_lifetime` |
| 32 | 4 | `min_short_window_seconds` |
| 36 | 4 | `min_long_window_seconds` |

types.name: MintCeilingArgs
docs: `MintCeilingArgs` (spec §4.2). Amounts are in base units.

types.name: MintConfig
docs: One configured mint slot on a `Treasury` (spec §3.1.1). 112 bytes.
| Offset | Size | Field |
| 0 | 32 | `mint` — `NATIVE_MINT` for SOL, `Pubkey::default()` if the slot is unused |
| 32 | 32 | `token_program` — SPL Token, Token-2022, or System program for native |
| 64 | 1 | `decimals` |
| 65 | 1 | `flags` — `MintFlags` bitfield |
| 72 | 40 | `ceiling` |

fields.name: _pad
docs: Named `_pad` in the spec; must stay zeroed.

types.name: MintLimit
docs: Per-mint spending limits an operator sets on a policy (spec §3.2.1). 96 bytes.
| Offset | Size | Field |
| 32 | 8 | `per_tx_max` |
| 40 | 8 | `short_window_max` |
| 48 | 4 | `short_window_seconds` |
| 52 | 8 | `long_window_max` |
| 60 | 4 | `long_window_seconds` |
| 64 | 8 | `lifetime_max` |
| 72 | 8 | `approval_threshold` (reserved v1.1) |
| 80 | 4 | `cooldown_seconds` (reserved v1.1) |
| 84 | 12 | `reserved` |

fields.name: lifetime_max
docs: Per session. `u64::MAX` means unlimited, and still has to fit under the ceiling.

fields.name: approval_threshold
docs: Reserved for v1.1. Must be 0 in v1.

fields.name: cooldown_seconds
docs: Reserved for v1.1. Must be 0 in v1.

types.name: MintLimitArgs
docs: `MintLimitArgs` (spec §4.2).
The v1.1 `approval_threshold` and `cooldown_seconds` fields are deliberately absent: the
program writes them as zero, so there is no way for a client to set a byte that a future
version will interpret differently.

types.name: PaymentExecuted
docs: One executed agent payment (spec §8).
`seq` and `audit_head` are what make the log verifiable: an indexer replays these
events ordered by `seq`, recomputes the chain with
`agent_rails_policy::next_audit_head`, and compares the terminus against
`AgentSession.audit_head`. A dropped, reordered, or forged event breaks the hash; a
dropped event is additionally visible as a gap in `seq` without hashing anything.

fields.name: seq
docs: The session sequence number *after* this payment, so the first is 1.

fields.name: amount
docs: Debited from the vault, before any Token-2022 transfer fee.

types.name: PaymentIntent
docs: `PaymentIntent` (spec §4.1) — the canonical `execute_payment` payload.
This is the whole agent-facing surface: an agent names a destination, an amount, and an
expiry, and the program decides. Two fields are load-bearing beyond the transfer itself.
`intent_id` is the idempotency key — it seeds the `IntentReceipt` PDA, so a retried
intent fails at account creation rather than paying twice (ADR-004). `expires_at` is
mandatory and short, so a stale intent cannot be resurrected later even after its
receipt has been closed.
In v1.1 signed-intent mode the signed message is
`DOMAIN_INTENT ‖ program_id ‖ treasury ‖ session ‖ borsh(PaymentIntent)`. The struct is
frozen now so v1 SDKs can already produce those bytes.

fields.name: intent_id
docs: Client-generated, UUIDv7 by default. Also the raw `IntentReceipt` seed.

fields.name: mint
docs: `NATIVE_MINT` selects the `execute_payment_sol` path and is rejected on the other.

fields.name: destination_owner
docs: Wallet owner. The destination token account is derived on-chain from this, never
passed in as a bare address, so an agent cannot be pointed at a look-alike account.

fields.name: amount
docs: Base units debited from the vault, before any Token-2022 transfer fee.

fields.name: expires_at
docs: Unix seconds; `now + [MIN_INTENT_TTL_SECONDS, MAX_INTENT_TTL_SECONDS]`.

fields.name: memo
docs: `≤ MAX_MEMO_LEN` bytes. Only `sha256(memo)` is stored, in the receipt.

types.name: Policy
docs: A named, operator-owned spending policy under one treasury (spec §3.2). 546 bytes.
| Offset | Size | Field |
| 0 | 8 | discriminator |
| 8 | 1 | `version` |
| 10 | 32 | `treasury` |
| 74 | 384 | `mint_limits` |
| 458 | 1 | `mint_count` |
| 459 | 1 | `destination_mode` |
| 460 | 1 | `require_memo` |
| 461 | 1 | `create_destination_ata` |
| 462 | 4 | `active_sessions` |
| 466 | 8 | `created_at` |
| 474 | 8 | `updated_at` |
| 482 | 64 | `reserved` |
PDA: `["policy", treasury, name]`.

fields.name: name
docs: 32-byte zero-padded UTF-8; also a seed component.

fields.name: destination_mode
docs: `DestinationMode`.

fields.name: create_destination_ata
docs: Requires the matching treasury ceiling flag.

fields.name: active_sessions
docs: Gates `close_policy`.

types.name: PolicyArgs
docs: `PolicyArgs` (spec §4.2) — the full rule set an operator writes in one instruction.
Passed whole rather than field by field so that `policy_leq_ceiling` can judge it as a
unit: whether a policy is legal depends on every limit *and* both destination flags
together, and a per-field setter would let an operator step through an illegal
intermediate state.

fields.name: mint_limits
docs: 1..=`MAX_MINTS` entries, each for a mint configured on the treasury.

fields.name: destination_mode
docs: `DestinationMode`.

fields.name: create_destination_ata
docs: Requires `Treasury.allow_create_destination_ata`.

types.name: PolicyClosed
docs: A policy account reclaimed. Carries no `limits_hash`: there are no `PolicyArgs` to
commit to, and the rules that were in force are already on record from `PolicyCreated`.

types.name: PolicyCreated
docs: A new named rule set under a treasury (spec §8).
`limits_hash` commits to the exact `PolicyArgs` the operator submitted, so an auditor
can prove which rules were in force at a point in time without the indexer having to
store every limit — and without trusting that a later `update_policy` did not rewrite
history.

types.name: PolicyUpdated
docs: A policy's rules rewritten in place (spec §8).
Carries *both* digests, per spec §5.2: `previous_limits_hash` lets an indexer verify it
has not missed a revision, the same way `AgentSession.seq` does for payments. The policy
address and `name` are stable across revisions, so the two chain cleanly.

types.name: ReceiptClosed
docs: A receipt reclaimed after `expires_at + RECEIPT_GRACE_SECONDS` (spec §8).
`treasury` is `Pubkey::default()`. `close_receipt` is permissionless and must succeed
after the session — and even the treasury — has been closed, so the instruction has
neither account. Indexers should route this variant on `session`.

types.name: SessionClosed
docs: The last word on a session's audit chain: after this the account is gone, and this event
is the only remaining on-chain proof of where the chain ended.

types.name: SessionRevoked
docs: Carries `seq` and `audit_head` so the chain has a witnessed terminus even if the session
account is closed before an indexer catches up.

types.name: SpendCounter
docs: Rolling spend state for one mint inside one session (spec §3.3.1). 80 bytes.
| Offset | Size | Field |
| 32 | 8 | `short_window_start` |
| 40 | 8 | `short_spent` |
| 48 | 8 | `long_window_start` |
| 56 | 8 | `long_spent` |
| 64 | 8 | `lifetime_spent` |
| 72 | 8 | `last_payment_at` |
Counters are looked up by `mint`, never by index, so reordering a policy's slots cannot
misattribute spend.

types.name: Treasury
docs: Cold-storage root of one treasury (spec §3.1). 944 bytes.
| Offset | Size | Field |
| 0 | 8 | discriminator |
| 8 | 1 | `version` |
| 10 | 1 | `sol_vault_bump` |
| 11 | 32 | `create_key` |
| 75 | 32 | `operator` |
| 107 | 160 | `guardians` |
| 267 | 1 | `guardian_count` |
| 269 | 8 | `paused_at` |
| 277 | 32 | `paused_by` |
| 309 | 1 | `allow_any_destination` |
| 310 | 1 | `allow_create_destination_ata` |
| 311 | 8 | `timelock_seconds` (reserved v1.1) |
| 319 | 32 | `recovery_destination` (reserved v1.1) |
| 799 | 1 | `mint_count` |
| 800 | 4 | `active_sessions` |
| 804 | 4 | `policy_count` |
| 808 | 8 | `created_at` |
| 816 | 128 | `reserved` |
PDA: `["treasury", create_key]`.

fields.name: create_key
docs: Ephemeral keypair that signed `create_treasury` once, then is never used again.
This is what allows unlimited treasuries per owner with no index bookkeeping.

fields.name: guardians
docs: Unused slots are `Pubkey::default()`.

fields.name: paused_at
docs: Unix seconds; 0 if never paused.

fields.name: allow_any_destination
docs: Ceiling flag for `DestinationMode::Any`.

fields.name: allow_create_destination_ata
docs: Ceiling flag for creating destination ATAs from the vault.

fields.name: timelock_seconds
docs: Reserved for v1.1. Must be 0 in v1.

fields.name: recovery_destination
docs: Reserved for v1.1. Timelock-exempt withdraw target, fixed at creation.

fields.name: active_sessions
docs: Non-revoked, non-closed sessions. Gates `close_treasury`.

fields.name: policy_count
docs: Open policies. Gates `close_treasury`.

types.name: Withdrawn
docs: Owner withdrawal of vault funds (spec §8). `destination` is the token account for SPL
and the system account for native SOL — the account that actually received the funds.
